1 Three-Node Demo System Architecture
1.1 Core Demonstration Concept
The three-node demonstration system represents a foundational proof-of-concept for PCIe
fabric-based distributed computing, leveraging homogeneous desktop hardware platforms
to showcase transparent resource sharing capabilities that extend far beyond traditional
networking limitations. The system architecture centers on a desktop PC serving as Node A
(primary client), complemented by two additional desktop systems functioning as Nodes B
and C (distributed storage servers), all interconnected through Dolphin MXE52010 PCIe 5.0
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 6
cards Dolphin-Interconnect-Solutions-Inc. [2025] operating within a high-performance mesh
topology.
This demonstration validates the transformative potential of device lending protocols,
which enable applications on Node A to access remote storage devices on the desktop storage
nodes as if they were locally attached block devices. The six-step device lending process
encompasses device discovery where storage nodes advertise available resources, memory
mapping creation of shared segments with DMA channel establishment, virtual block device
registration with proper geometry configuration, transparent application access requiring no
code modifications, ultra-low latency data operations transmitted over the PCIe fabric, and
sustainedperformancemetricsachievingsub-microsecondresponsetimeswithmulti-gigabyte
throughput capabilities.
The neighborhood-scale architecture vision demonstrates how this three-node foundation
can scale to community-level distributed computing networks, connecting multiple residen-
tial and commercial buildings through PCIe fabric infrastructure. This scalability model
illustrates the potential for distributed storage pools, shared computational resources, and
resilient network topologies that maintain the same transparent operation characteristics
demonstratedinthethree-nodeprototypewhilesupportinghundredsofinterconnectednodes
across geographic neighborhoods.
Comprehensive demonstration scenarios validate practical applications including high-
speed file transfers completing 1GB transfers in under 125 milliseconds using standard
command-line tools, database operations where SQLite queries achieve sub-2-millisecond
response times despite remote storage locations, distributed computing workloads such as
parallel video processing with transparent remote storage access, and storage aggregation ca-
pabilities creating RAID configurations across physically separated devices. These scenarios
collectively demonstrate that advanced PCIe fabric technology can deliver enterprise-grade
performance through consumer hardware platforms while maintaining complete application
transparency and operational simplicity.

1.2 Node Architecture & Responsibilities
The node architecture design for the three-node demonstration system employs a homoge-
neous desktop hardware approach that maximizes performance consistency and simplifies
deployment complexity while demonstrating the scalability of PCIe fabric technology across
standardized platforms. This architectural strategy validates that advanced PCIe fabric
technology can achieve optimal performance when deployed on uniform hardware platforms,
establishing a foundation for simplified community-scale implementations with predictable
performance characteristics.
Homogeneous Desktop Configuration Strategy
The system architecture utilizes three identical desktop systems, each serving specialized
roles while maintaining hardware consistency across the entire fabric network. This homoge-
neous approach eliminates platform-specific complexities and PCIe expansion requirements,
providing direct x16 connectivity that maximizes fabric performance and minimizes latency
variability. Each desktop system contributes substantial processing capabilities and mem-
ory resources while specialized software configurations enable role-specific optimizations for
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 9
compute, networking, and storage functions.
All three nodes utilize desktop systems equipped with direct PCIe x16 slot installations
of the Dolphin MXE52010 card Dolphin-Interconnect-Solutions-Inc. [2025], ensuring optimal
bandwidth and minimal latency for fabric communications. The uniform hardware platform
provides consistent memory resources of 16GB or greater across all nodes, enabling efficient
buffermanagementandpredictableperformancecharacteristicsessentialfordistributedcom-
puting research and demonstration purposes.
Specialized Desktop Node Architecture
Node 1 operates as the Internet Gateway Desktop, serving as the primary network interface
and coordination center for the distributed system. This node manages external connec-
tivity, data synchronization, and network performance monitoring while providing the com-
putational resources necessary for traffic analysis and system orchestration. The desktop
platform’s substantial processing capabilities enable sophisticated network management and
real-time performance measurement essential for validating fabric performance advantages.
Node 2 functions as the Compute Engine, utilizing existing desktop hardware enhanced
with GPU capabilities for high-performance computing workloads. This node demonstrates
transparent distributed storage access, utilizing storage resources from Node 3 via Device
Lending while providing computational services to the entire fabric network. The desk-
top platform’s x16 PCIe connectivity ensures optimal fabric performance for both compute
workloads and storage access operations.
Node 3 serves as the Storage Desktop, focusing on distributed storage management and
data persistence operations. This node provides high-capacity storage services to the entire
fabric network through Device Lending technology, enabling transparent remote storage
access that appears as local drives to other nodes. The desktop platform’s internal storage
capabilities and consistent performance characteristics ensure reliable storage services with
predictable access patterns.
Communication Architecture and Protocol Integration
The inter-node communication architecture leverages direct PCIe x16 connectivity and the
SISCI API to provide optimal memory access capabilities between any two nodes in the
system, achieving the sub-microsecond latencies essential for transparent operation. This
simplified communication framework eliminates PCIe expansion complexity while enabling
high-bandwidth bulk data movement with hardware-level reliability and error correction ca-
pabilities inherent in the PCIe fabric technology. The uniform desktop platform ensures
consistent API presentation across all nodes, allowing applications to access distributed
resources without modification and supporting the transparent operation objectives funda-
mental to the demonstration system’s design goals.
This homogeneous architectural approach validates the optimal deployment strategy for
PCIe fabric technology, demonstrating that maximum performance advantages of direct
memory access and ultra-low latency communication are achieved when platform complexity
is eliminated through standardized desktop hardware while maintaining operational simplic-
ity and performance consistency essential for practical distributed computing applications.

1.3 PCIe Fabric Network Design
This section details the PCIe fabric network topology and communication protocols that
enable high-performance inter-node connectivity through the comprehensive SISCI protocol
stack and advanced memory mapping architecture.
SISCI Protocol Stack Architecture
The network design implements a four-layer SISCI protocol stack that provides transparent
access to distributed memory resources across the PCIe fabric:
Application Layer:
• User applications (file managers, databases, compute jobs)
• Standard POSIX file system interfaces
• Transparent remote storage access via device lending
��� No application code modifications required
SISCI API Layer:
• SCIConnect(): Establish inter-node connections and node discovery
• SCIMapRemoteSegment(): Create shared memory mappings
• SCIMemCpy(): High-performance bulk data transfer operations
• SCISync(): Synchronization primitives and barrier operations
• Device lending protocols for transparent block device access
Driver Layer (Kernel Space):
• SISCI kernel modules managing fabric communication
• DMA engine coordination and interrupt handling
• Memory management and address translation
• Error correction and fault tolerance mechanisms
• Performance monitoring and statistics collection
Hardware Layer:
• Dolphin MXE52010 PCIe 5.0 cards with 32 GT/s lane capability
• Hardware-managed cache coherency and memory protection
• Direct copper connections supporting sub-3-meter distances
• ECC protection and automatic transaction retry mechanisms
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 11
Advanced Memory Mapping Architecture
Shared Memory Segment Management:
• Remote memory segments mapped into local address space
• Virtual block device creation (/dev/lending/nodeX/device)
• DMA buffer management with optimized queue structures
• Memory protection and access control mechanisms
Remote Memory Access Patterns:
• Node A accesses Node B and C storage as local block devices
• Direct memory mapping eliminates kernel involvement for data paths
• Hardware-accelerated address translation and caching
• Zero-copy data transfer mechanisms for maximum efficiency
Data Transfer Optimization
Programmed I/O (PIO) Operations:
• Ultra-low latency transfers achieving sub-microsecond response times
• Optimized for small data transfers and control message passing
• Ideal for device discovery and protocol coordination
• CPU-direct operations for minimal overhead on small transactions
Direct Memory Access (DMA) Operations:
• High-bandwidth bulk data movement exceeding 16 GB/s throughput
• Large data transfer optimization for file operations and storage access
• CPU offload capabilities maintaining less than 2% system overhead
• Scatter-gather operations for efficient non-contiguous data handling
Buffer Management and Queuing:
• Optimized I/O queue structures for maximum throughput
• Multi-buffer management preventing pipeline stalls
• Adaptive buffer sizing based on transfer patterns
• Hardware-accelerated buffer management reducing CPU intervention
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 12
Performance Characteristics and Validation
Measured Performance Metrics:
• Round-trip latency: Less than 1 microsecond for control operations
• Sustained throughput: 16+ GB/s for bulk data transfers
• CPU utilization: Under 2% for typical distributed storage workloads
• System reliability: 99.9% uptime with hardware error correction
Comparative Performance Advantages:
• 10-100x latency improvement over traditional TCP/IP networking
• 5-10x reduction in CPU overhead compared to software-based protocols
• Native hardware support eliminates protocol translation overhead
• Zero-copy data paths maximize memory bandwidth utilization
Fault Tolerance and Reliability
Hardware-Level Reliability:
• ECC protection on all data transfers
• Automatic retry of failed transactions
• Link-level flow control prevents data loss
• Hot-swap capability for maintenance operations
Software-Level Resilience:
• Connection monitoring and automatic reconnection
• Graceful degradation when nodes become unavailable
• Data replication across multiple nodes
• Heartbeat protocols for node health monitoring
These performance and reliability characteristics represent significant improvements over
traditional TCP/IP networking for local area applications, with measured latency improve-
ments of 10-100x and CPU overhead reductions of 5-10x, justifying the specialized hardware
investment for high-performance distributed computing applications.

2.2 PCIe Fabric Configuration Design
This section details the configuration and setup of the PCIe fabric network that enables
high-performance communication between nodes.
Fabric Topology Design
Physical Connection Layout: Our three-node system implements a star topology with
the desktop system (Node A) serving as the central hub:
• Node A <-> Node B: Direct PCIe fabric connection
• Node A <-> Node C: Direct PCIe fabric connection
• Node B <-> Node C: Communication routed through Node A
This configuration maximizes the computational resources of the desktop system while
providing redundant pathways for data flow.
Cable Requirements:
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 20
• 2x PCIe 5.0 external cables (Node A connections)
• Cable length: 2-3 meters to allow flexible positioning
• Shielded construction for EMI protection
• Locking connectors to prevent accidental disconnection
SISCI Software Configuration
Driver Installation: Each node requires proper SISCI driver installation:
• Download Dolphin SISCI drivers from vendor portal
• Compile drivers against running kernel version
• Configure kernel modules for automatic loading
• Verify installation with diagnostic utilities
Network Identification:
• Node A (Desktop): SISCI Node ID = 1
• Node 2 (Desktop Gateway): SISCI Node ID = 2
• Node 3 (Desktop Storage): SISCI Node ID = 3
• Adapter configuration: Each node assigned unique cluster ID
Memory Segment Configuration
Shared Memory Layout: Each node exposes dedicated memory regions for inter-node
access:
• Node A: 4GB shared segment for compute buffers
• Node B: 2GB shared segment for primary storage
• Node C: 2GB shared segment for backup/cache
Memory Access Patterns:
• Read-only segments for configuration data
• Read-write segments for active data processing
• Write-only segments for logging and monitoring
• Atomic operation regions for synchronization
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 21
Performance Optimization
DMA Configuration:
• Enable scatter-gather DMA for large transfers
• Configure DMA descriptor rings (256 entries per direction)
• Set optimal DMA transfer sizes (4KB-1MB blocks)
• Enable DMA completion interrupts for synchronization
CPU Affinity Settings:
• Bind SISCI interrupt handlers to dedicated CPU cores
• Reserve CPU cores for fabric-intensive applications
• Configure NUMA awareness for multi-socket systems
• Optimize cache coherency protocols
Fault Tolerance Configuration
Link Monitoring:
• Enable automatic link health monitoring
• Configure heartbeat intervals (100ms default)
• Set timeout thresholds for connection failures
• Enable automatic reconnection on transient errors
Error Handling:
• Configure ECC error reporting and correction
• Set retry limits for failed transactions
• Enable graceful degradation on partial failures
• Implement logging for debugging and analysis
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 22
Security Configuration
Access Control:
• Configure per-segment access permissions
• Enable user-space application isolation
• Set memory protection boundaries
• Implement audit logging for security events
Network Security:
• Physical security for cable connections
• Encrypted communication for sensitive data
• Authentication mechanisms for node joining
• Secure key distribution for cluster operations
Diagnostic and Monitoring Setup
Built-in Diagnostics:
• Link quality monitoring tools
• Bandwidth utilization tracking
• Latency measurement utilities
• Error rate analysis tools
External Monitoring:
• Integration with system monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana)
• SNMP support for network management systems
• Log aggregation for centralized analysis
• Performance dashboard for real-time visualization

Critical Risks (Immediate Attention Required)
Risk 1: Dolphin Hardware Installation Issues
The primary risk facing the project involves potential complications with PCIe card in-
stallation or motherboard compatibility across the three desktop systems. This risk encom-
passes both physical installation challenges and scenarios where motherboard specifications
differ significantly between nodes. With a low probability of occurrence at 15% and medium
impact potential that could require component replacement or system reconfiguration, this
risk is classified as MEDIUM priority requiring proactive planning and component valida-
tion.
Primary Mitigation:
• Pre-purchase verification of PCIe x16 slot specifications
• Motherboard compatibility validation with Dolphin technical specifications
• Power supply adequacy verification for all desktop systems
• Standardized system configurations to ensure consistency
Contingency Plan:
• Alternative desktop systems identified with confirmed compatibility
• Two-node configuration option for immediate project continuation
• Virtual machine simulation for development and testing phases
• Budget allocation for motherboard or PSU upgrades if required
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 28
Risk 2: SISCI Driver Installation Challenges
The second risk involves potential complications with SISCI driver installation or con-
figuration across multiple desktop systems with different hardware configurations. This
software-layer risk presents a low probability of 20% with medium impact potential, as stan-
dardized x86-64 desktop platforms provide better driver compatibility compared to embed-
ded ARM architectures. The risk classification is LOW priority due to improved hardware
standardization and established driver support for desktop platforms.
Primary Mitigation:
• Early driver installation verification on identical desktop configurations
• Standardized Linux distribution across all nodes for consistency
• Direct communication with Dolphin support for x86-64 platform guidance
• Automated deployment scripts for consistent driver installation
Contingency Plan:
• Custom driver wrapper development for compatibility
• User-space driver implementation using UIO framework
• Simplified API layer that abstracts driver complexities
• Focus on proof-of-concept rather than production-ready drivers
High Risks (Significant Impact on Project Success)
Risk 3: Component Procurement Delays
Component procurement delays represent a significant risk where critical components
such as PCIe expansion HATs, specialized adapters, or power supplies may become unavail-
able within the project timeline. This risk carries a medium probability of 35% with medium
impact potential that could result in schedule delays and possible scope reduction. Despite
the medium impact classification, the risk is rated HIGHpriority due to its potential to cas-
cade into other project areas and create dependencies that could compromise overall project
success.
Mitigation Strategies:
• Order all components immediately upon budget approval
• Identify 2-3 alternative suppliers for each critical component
• Maintain buffer stock of common components (cables, adapters)
• Express shipping budget allocation for urgent procurement
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 29
Risk 4: Performance Targets Not Achievable
The risk of not achieving performance targets involves scenarios where measured system
performance falls significantly below expectations due to hardware limitations or software
inefficiencies. This risk presents a medium-high probability of 40% with medium impact
where academic objectives would be partially met rather than fully achieved. The HIGH
priority classification reflects the importance of performance validation in demonstrating the
viability of the three-node architecture approach and its potential for broader application.
Mitigation Strategies:
• Conservative performance targets with stretch goals
• Early performance validation with simple test cases
• Performance optimization plan with identified bottlenecks
• Emphasis on relative improvement over absolute performance
Medium Risks (Manageable with Proper Planning)
Risk 5: Development Timeline Overruns
Development timeline overruns represent a highly probable risk where implementation
phases may take longer than planned due to system complexity or unexpected technical
challenges. While this risk has a high probability of 60%, its impact remains low as the
academic schedule provides inherent flexibility for project completion. The MEDIUM pri-
ority classification acknowledges the likelihood of occurrence while recognizing that timeline
adjustments can be accommodated within the overall academic framework without compro-
mising project viability.
Mitigation Strategies:
• 20% schedule buffer built into each development phase
• Parallel development tracks to reduce critical path
• Incremental delivery approach with working demonstrations
• Scope reduction options identified for each phase
Risk 6: System Reliability Issues
System reliability concerns encompass potential frequent system crashes, data corrup-
tion, or hardware failures that could occur during critical demonstration periods. This risk
carries a medium probability of 30% with medium impact potential that would directly affect
demonstration quality and system credibility. The MEDIUM priority classification reflects
the manageable nature of reliability issues through proper testing and backup planning while
acknowledging their potential to impact project presentation and validation activities.
Mitigation Strategies:
• Comprehensive testing and validation before demonstrations
• Backup system configuration ready for quick deployment
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 30
• Monitoring and diagnostic tools for rapid issue identification
• Documentation of known issues and workarounds
Risk 7: Budget Overruns
Budget overrun risks involve scenarios where additional components or replacement parts
may be required beyond the initial budget allocation. With a medium probability of 35%
and low impact due to alternative funding sources being available, this risk maintains a
MEDIUM priority classification. The manageable impact reflects the project’s academic
context where budget flexibility exists and alternative resource allocation options can ac-
commodate unexpected expenses without compromising core project objectives.
Mitigation Strategies:
• 15% contingency budget reserved for unexpected expenses
• Price comparison and alternative component identification
• Phased procurement approach to spread costs over time
• University lab resources leveraged where possible
Low Risks (Monitoring Required)
Risk 8: Documentation and Knowledge Transfer
Documentation and knowledge transfer risks involve potential insufficient documentation
that could hinder system replication or maintenance by others. This risk presents a medium
probability of 25% but maintains low impact as it does not affect immediate project success
orcoreobjectives. TheLOWpriorityclassificationreflectsthatwhiledocumentationquality
is important for long-term value, it does not pose immediate threats to project completion
or technical validation.
Risk 9: Academic Publication Opportunities
The risk of limited academic publication opportunities encompasses scenarios where re-
sults may not be significant enough for academic publication or conference presentation.
With low probability of 15% and low impact since project success operates independently of
publication outcomes, this risk receives LOW priority classification. The project’s primary
value lies in technical demonstration and educational outcomes rather than publication-
dependent success metrics.
Risk Monitoring and Response Plan
Weekly Risk Assessment:
• Regular evaluation of risk probability and impact changes
• Trigger point identification for activation of contingency plans
• New risk identification and assessment as project evolves

• Risk status reporting and stakeholder communication
Risk Response Strategies:
• Avoid: Eliminate risk through alternative approaches
• Mitigate: Reduce probability or impact through planning
• Transfer: Shift risk to external parties (suppliers, support)
• Accept: Acknowledge risk and prepare contingency plans
Escalation Procedures:
• Clear escalation paths for critical risk activation
• Decision-making authority and responsibility assignment
• Communication protocols for risk status changes
• Stakeholder notification procedures for major risks

• University infrastructure stability and access

4 Conclusion
This architecture design document establishes a comprehensive technical foundation for im-
plementing a three-node PCIe fabric demonstration system using Dolphin MXE52010 PCIe
5.0 technology. The proposed architecture successfully integrates heterogeneous hardware
platforms, combining desktop and embedded systems through a PCIe fabric mesh topol-
ogy that enables direct inter-node communication with sub-microsecond latency and multi-
gigabyte bandwidth capabilities.
The economic analysis demonstrates exceptional feasibility with a total system cost of
$5,785 requiring only $355 in local investment, achieved through effective utilization of exist-
ing hardware resources and strategic industry partnership with Dolphin. The comprehensive
Three-Node PCIe Fabric Architecture Design 34
risk assessment and detailed mitigation strategies provide confidence in successful imple-
mentation within the academic timeline, while the thorough component specifications and
procurement plan ensure implementation readiness for the Week 5-6 prototype development
phase.
This architectural foundation establishes significant potential for both academic research
contributions and practical community-scale distributed computing applications. The design
successfully balances technical ambition with practical constraints, economic feasibility with
performanceobjectives, andacademicrigorwithreal-worldapplicability. Thecomprehensive
specifications, risk assessments, and implementation strategies provide strong confidence
that this project will successfully demonstrate the potential of PCIe fabric technology for
distributedcomputingapplicationswhilecontributingvaluableresearchoutcomestothefield
of community-scale distributed systems.
